CCFRec (KDD 2025) closely matches the representation problem: simple ID/text addition or concatenation can leave textual and collaborative semantics misaligned. It uses fine-grained semantic codes, code-guided cross-attention, masked-code prediction, and masked-sequence alignment to learn correlations among item components and interaction patterns. Its published implementation uses pretrained Sentence-T5, so it supplies architectural inspiration rather than a directly admissible from-scratch recipe. [Paper](https://www.atailab.cn/seminar2025Fall/pdf/2025-KDD-Bridging%20Textual-Collaborative%20Gap%20through%20Semantic%20Codes%20for%20Sequential%20Recommendation.pdf)

JEPA4Rec (COLM 2025) encodes item descriptions with a bidirectional Transformer and combines language masking, prediction of complete item representations, and sequence–item contrastive learning. Its relevant contribution is supervision at both token and item levels, aimed at learning preference-relevant representations with limited pretraining data. This does not establish that the published system satisfies the present no-pretrained-weights constraint. [Paper](https://openreview.net/pdf?id=0Qbwjd0fxB)

A constraint-compatible hypothesis, inferred from these methods: retain masked-item BERT4Rec, jointly train a small title/description encoder from random initialization, and fuse its output with item-ID embeddings through a nonlinear gate or cross-attention. Token interactions could represent specific feature combinations beyond bag-of-words associations; that remains an experimental hypothesis. Train the fused representation through masked-item prediction, optionally adding text reconstruction or ID–text alignment within the same network. Mask every target’s identity and text together to prevent leakage; use appended-mask inference and one checkpoint per category. The located papers do not establish gains under this exact benchmark or prove compositional preference generalization.
